styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Nyhavn, the palaces and Tivoli in the old centre.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Smørrebrød, bakeries and the Nørrebro food scene.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Castles, Viking ships and the old harbour.

stays.why: Walk to Nyhavn, Tivoli, the palaces and the Round Tower. Best for a first short visit.
Next to the central station and Tivoli; lively food and bar streets. Easy airport trains.
Cheaper, young and multicultural. Good cafés and street food; 10–15 min by bike or metro to the centre.
Quiet, leafy and close to the Little Mermaid, the lakes and the park. Good for families.

food: Start with smørrebrød: rye bread with herring, egg and shrimp. Lunch portions are bigger than they look.
Try a bakery 'kanelsnegl' (cinnamon roll) and Danish pastries; they are cheapest to take away.
Rejsekort or the app for cheap eats: hot dogs from a pølsevogn stand cost about DKK 30–45.
Nørrebro and Vesterbro have the best value: falafel, shawarma and street food halls, about DKK 60–100 a meal.
Book dinner ahead on weekends. A sit-down dinner with drinks often runs DKK 250–450 per person.
more_time: Swap a city day for Roskilde: the Viking Ship Museum and the cathedral, about 25 min by S-train.
Take the train to Louisiana Museum of Modern Art north of the city; check opening days on the day.
Cross to Malmö, Sweden, by train over the Øresund bridge for a half-day change of scene.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the old centre, a museum or two and a proper food day, with time for a harbour boat.

month_notes: Jan: cold, highs near 4°C, 13 rain days. Pack a warm coat and waterproof shoes.
Feb: still cold at 5°C, slightly drier with 11 rain days. Short daylight; plan indoor sights.
Mar: cool at 7°C, 11 rain days. Layers and an umbrella help.
Apr: milder, around 10°C, 9 rain days. Good for walking and parks.
May: pleasant at 15°C, 10 rain days. Great month for bikes and the harbour.
Jun: mild at 19°C, 10 rain days. Long evenings; book popular restaurants.
Jul: warmest at 20°C but 13 rain days. Carry a light rain jacket.
Aug: similar at 21°C, 12 rain days. Busy season; book hotels early.
Sep: still mild at 18°C, 12 rain days. Fewer crowds, good for museums.
Oct: cooler at 13°C, 13 rain days. Bring a waterproof layer.
Nov: chilly at 8°C, 12 rain days. Dark early; plan cosy indoor days.
Dec: cold at 6°C, 13 rain days. Christmas markets and lights; dress warm.

climate_guide.summary: Cool coastal climate: mild summers, cold winters, and rain in every month. Pack layers and a rain jacket.

items.title: Best time: May to September
items.text: Highs of 15–21°C and long days. Best for walking, bikes and the harbour.

items.title: Rain all year
items.text: 9–13 rain days every month. Showers pass quickly; a light waterproof beats an umbrella in wind.

items.title: Winter is cold and dark
items.text: December to February highs of 4–6°C, lows near 1°C. Daylight is short; plan indoor sights.

items.title: Windy by the water
items.text: The harbour and canals feel colder than the forecast. A windproof layer helps.

items.title: Summers are mild, not hot
items.text: July and August peak around 20–21°C. Rarely need air-conditioning.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers, a waterproof jacket and comfortable shoes for cobblestones. Add a warm hat and gloves in winter.

transit.best: Metro and S-trains for most trips; rent a bike for short hops in good weather.

modes.text: Runs 24/7. M1/M2 link the airport to the centre in about 14 min.
S-trains and buses cover the city; a 3-zone ticket costs about DKK 30.
Buses fill the gaps the trains miss. Same ticket zones apply.
Taxis are metered and pricey. Uber and Bolt operate in the city.
Driving in the centre is slow and parking is costly. Park outside and take transit.
The city is flat and bike-friendly; rental bikes are everywhere.
Harbour buses and small ferries cross the canals cheaply.
The old centre is compact and easy on foot; cobblestones need comfy shoes.
